detailed_rationale:
Welspun Living, the home-textiles arm of the Welspun Group (bed/bath linens, rugs, and a newer flooring vertical under brands including Christy, Spaces and Disney Home), had a genuinely weak FY26. Full-year sales fell to Rs 9,399 Cr from Rs 10,545 Cr (-11%), and net profit collapsed to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 644 Cr (-67%), with operating margin compressing to 8% from 12% a year earlier. The quarterly cadence makes clear this was not a one-quarter blip: Q1-Q3 FY26 profit ran at just Rs 89 Cr, Rs 15 Cr and Rs 3 Cr respectively (versus Rs 123-133 Cr a year earlier), before a partial Q4 FY26 recovery to Rs 106 Cr. We also flag a genuine one-off: Q3 FY26 carried an unusually high ~82% effective tax rate versus a normal 25-28%, which exaggerated that quarter's profit collapse and should be looked through when judging the underlying trend (though even adjusting for it, the pretax trend was still soft).

Home textiles (92% of revenue) is directly exposed to US/EU consumer demand and retailer inventory cycles -- the pattern here (soft toplines, margin compression, exports-driven business) is consistent with a demand-and-cost-pressure cycle in Western home-goods retail rather than anything Welspun-specific, but it is a real earnings deterioration regardless of cause. Debt has come down modestly (Rs 2,762 Cr to Rs 2,315 Cr), and management sold down its captive power subsidiary stake to an affiliate for incremental cash, a minor positive for balance-sheet flexibility but not transformative. Promoter holding has drifted down from 70.5% to 66.4% over three years -- flagged, though not at a level we would call alarming on its own.

At a live PE near 68-77x on a badly depressed earnings base, the stock is expensive on any reasonable normalized-earnings view; the market appears to be looking through FY26 to a recovery that has not yet shown up convincingly in the print (the Q4 recovery to Rs 106 Cr profit is still well below the year-ago Rs 133 Cr).
recommendation_rationale: Hold, following the quant score -- we see nothing here that would justify converting this into anything more constructive than Hold, and while the fundamentals argue for real caution (this is one of the weaker prints in this batch), the quant score already sits at Hold and the asymmetric-override rule does not let us force a Sell; we note the tension honestly through a conservative growth number and a direct negative_para instead.
summary: Welspun Living, a leading Indian home-textiles exporter (bed and bath linens, rugs, and a newer flooring business), had a difficult FY26: sales fell about 11% and profit fell about 67% as margins compressed sharply, with one quarter's results distorted further by an unusually high tax rate. Debt has come down modestly. The stock currently trades at a rich earnings multiple given how depressed current profitability is. We rate it a Hold, but flag this as one of the weaker fundamental trends we reviewed this round.
positive_para: The company retains genuine scale and brand relationships in global home textiles (Christy, Spaces, Disney Home licensing), has trimmed debt modestly year-on-year, and showed a partial profit recovery in Q4 FY26 (Rs 106 Cr, up from a Rs 3 Cr trough in Q3). The flooring diversification (8% of revenue and growing) gives the business a second leg if home-textiles demand stays soft.
negative_para: FY26 was a genuinely weak year -- sales down 11%, profit down 67%, margins compressed from the mid-teens to high single digits -- and even adjusting for the one-off high-tax quarter, the underlying trend through nine months was soft. A live PE in the high 60s/70s on this depressed earnings base is not a cheap entry point; the stock needs a real, multi-quarter margin recovery just to justify the current price, and export-facing home textiles remains exposed to Western consumer demand and freight/input-cost cycles outside the company's control.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A PE in the high 60s/70s sitting on top of a profit base that just fell 67% implies the market is confidently pricing a strong multi-year recovery back toward FY25-level margins (12%+) and beyond. Nothing in the current print proves that recovery is underway yet -- Q4 FY26 profit is still below the year-ago quarter. This looks rich relative to demonstrated earnings power; we would want to see 2-3 quarters of genuine margin recovery before agreeing the multiple is earned.
